name: dag-workflow
description: Dependency-ordered DAG workflows of Claude Code subagents, with a live DAG pane

session_learning.title: Learn skills across user sessions
session_learning.description: Learn reusable skills from user turns and tool outcomes across the whole session, including work outside DAGs; background Sonnet usage is billed to your Claude plan

learning_interval.title: Tool calls between background learning
learning_interval.description: Start learning at a worker turn boundary after this many tool calls; a completed user-requested main turn also flushes pending experience

learning_min_opportunities.title: Unused skill exposure limit
learning_min_opportunities.description: Archive managed skills after this many eligible user prompts without a successful Skill or Read call

learning_max_skills.title: Managed skills per project
learning_max_skills.description: Target active learned-skill capacity per project; skills with no eligible exposure remain protected

learning_max_input_chars.title: Maximum learning input characters
learning_max_input_chars.description: Total background learning prompt size, including instructions, evidence and complete editable skill bodies

learning_max_daily_runs.title: Automatic learning attempts per UTC day
learning_max_daily_runs.description: Shared across all user sessions; reserves an attempt before automatic learning starts. A user-typed /dag learn bypasses this counter, not the input limit

learning_retention_days.title: Learning data retention days
learning_retention_days.description: Remove old inactive session evidence and expired archived managed skills at startup or /dag learning prune; 0 keeps them, active skills and running batches are protected

auto_recovery.title: Automatic node recovery
auto_recovery.description: Use confident Jev failure classification to retry within the original scope, at most two extra attempts per node; implementation fixes may use Opus. A reviewer FAIL verdict is never retried: once per run the producers its findings cite rerun with them, then the reviewers

jev_enabled.title: Jev automatic decisions
jev_enabled.description: With TYPESAFE_API_KEY, classify DAG workers and resolve uncertain tool permissions; missing or uncertain decisions retain the existing flow

jev_max_calls.title: Jev calls per loaded session
jev_max_calls.description: Maximum combined HTTP and session-model decision calls, including failed calls and fallback parts; identical in-flight requests share a call. At the limit, permissions retain the host decision, routing retains the proposal, and automatic recovery stops

jev_model_fallback.title: Jev session-model fallback
jev_model_fallback.description: When TYPESAFE_API_KEY is missing or the Jev API fails, times out or returns an error, ask the session's own Sonnet model instead; its usage counts against your Claude plan

jev_confidence.title: Jev minimum confidence
jev_confidence.description: Minimum confidence for automatic category assignment from the Jev API and for every tool permission or recovery decision

jev_model_routing_confidence.title: Jev session-model routing confidence
jev_model_routing_confidence.description: Minimum confidence for applying a category the session model chose (without TYPESAFE_API_KEY or when the Jev API fails); permission and recovery decisions keep Jev minimum confidence

jev_permission_scope.title: Jev permission scope
jev_permission_scope.description: dag (default): limits Jev permission decisions to tool calls made by DAG node workers, leaving the main conversation's prompts unchanged; all: Jev resolves every uncertain tool permission, including the main conversation's, and sends the tool input to Jev

enforcement.title: DAG enforcement
enforcement.description: auto: Jev decides per request; small requests run directly in the main conversation and requests that need three or more nodes run as DAGs under the strict rules; strict: the main conversation may only plan, read and orchestrate, and all work runs in DAG nodes; guide: only instruct; off: no enforcement

start_approval.title: Approve runs before they start
start_approval.description: always: a run the model starts in an interactive session waits until you approve it in the /dag pane or with /dag approve; off: runs start at once

anti_slop_scan.title: Anti-slop scan after edits
anti_slop_scan.description: After Edit or Write, scan added lines and precise TS/JS test changes, including advisory expectation replacements and explicit real-API substitutions; show candidates to the model with no model call

secure_scan.title: Semgrep secure-coding scan
secure_scan.description: When semgrep is on PATH, run the KISA rules in skills/secure-coding/rules on what each Edit or Write adds (a block rule such as a hard-coded secret refuses the call before it lands; other hits come back as context), and give every hit on a run's change its own verifier in review.security. Without semgrep nothing runs

trajectory_log.title: Trajectory log
trajectory_log.description: Record every run's trajectory under .claude/dag/trajectories/ for comparing runs: each node attempt's exact prompt, model, answer, verification, reviewer notes, change against HEAD, token counts and tool-call transcript, each review-fix round's findings, and the main conversation's turns. Secrets are masked and long text is cut. Each settled run is also joined into <run_id>.jsonl. Startup removes old and excess trajectories by trajectory_retention_days and trajectory_max_mb, whether or not the log is on; retention_days does not apply to them

trajectory_retention_days.title: Trajectory retention (days)
trajectory_retention_days.description: At startup, remove the trajectory (folder and joined .jsonl) of a settled run, or of another session's main conversation, whose newest file is older than this many days; the current session and runs that have not settled are kept. 0 keeps everything

trajectory_max_mb.title: Trajectory size cap (MB)
trajectory_max_mb.description: At startup, when .claude/dag/trajectories/ holds more than this many megabytes, remove settled runs' trajectories (and other sessions' main conversations), the one with the oldest newest file first, until it fits or only the current session and unsettled runs are left. A folder of more than 2000 files is skipped. 0 means no cap

review_ledger.title: Review fix ledger
review_ledger.description: In the automatic review-fix round, keep each failed reviewer's findings and a copy of the producers' files before the fix. When review-spec and review-standards run again they get those findings and the fix's diff, judge their own findings RESOLVED or OPEN, accept changes made to resolve any finding, and fail only on an open finding or a new one on a line the fix changed; other new findings go under ## Deferred. The producer is told that a finding on its files concerns it even beyond its original task. Off keeps the reviewers' original prompts

anti_slop_skip.title: Anti-slop patterns to skip
anti_slop_skip.description: Pattern ids the scan never reports, such as unreasoned-assertion in a repository that allows casts without a SAFETY comment

main_allowed_tools.title: Extra main-conversation tools
main_allowed_tools.description: Tool names the main conversation may still call under strict enforcement, besides the read-only and orchestration tools

language.title: DAG pane language
language.description: Language of the DAG pane: en or ko

max_concurrent.title: Parallel nodes per run
max_concurrent.description: How many nodes of one DAG run may run at the same time

node_messages.title: Node hand-back messages
node_messages.description: compact: the main session gets a short progress note instead of each finished node's full report (kept in the run snapshot); full: keep Claude Code's default hand-back

retention_days.title: Checkpoint retention (days)
retention_days.description: Settled runs from other sessions older than this, with their reports, plus stale context, decision and session records, are pruned at startup; 0 keeps everything
